An iron bar of length L has magnetic moment M. It is bent at the middle of its length such that the two
arms make an angle 60° with each other. The magnetic moment of this new magnet is :
(1)
M
(2)
2 M
(3)
2M
(4)
3 M
Moving Charges and Magnetism
subject: Physics
b6_reason: Pole strength is unchanged and the bent arms with a 60 degree opening put the poles L/2 apart, so the new moment is M/2 - matching option 2 only if its flattened '2 M' means M/2.
b6_working: m = M/L. Each arm length L/2, so each arm moment = M/2. The two moment vectors are at 180 - 60 = 120 degrees, resultant = 2*(M/2)*cos(60) = M/2. Equivalently the arms and the pole-to-pole line form an equilateral triangle of side L/2, so M' = m*(L/2) = M/2.
b6_note: Damaged options: radicals/fraction bars lost, so option 2 '$2\,M$' and option 4 '$3\,M$' could be M/2 and M/3 or sqrt(2)M and sqrt(3)M. My computed value M/2 exists in the list only under the first reading; under the second reading no option is correct. Flagged for human check of the option LaTeX.
